# Overview of MicroDuck Task Demonstration

This is demonstrated by splitting into tasks. The GPU and BPU videos in each notebook correspond to the same task. Expand the items to view the complete task list and additional versions.

**Video Description:** GPU GIF shows the policy reasoning reproduction saved in the Notebook; BPU GIF shows the closed loop records of policy reasoning execution on RDK X5 and simulation running on Ubuntu. When generating a new BPU video, run the corresponding unit and connect the HBM, RDK service, and simulation workstation. The browser perturbation demonstration applies external force through mouse dragging; the ladder Notebook shows the step contact phase, and the step-by-step climbing demonstration can be reproduced in the community below.

The above 7 notebooks store the execution counts and outputs of 64 code units. The complete execution snapshot is in the notebook; to avoid duplicating large MP4 files, the video output is replaced with a compressed GIF linked to this directory. The running status and optional steps can be found in [ Notebook description ](../../03-Notebook/README.md).

## Ladder Climbing: Step on the rungs progressively

The community reproduction video shows the ducklings stepping onto the ladder rungs step by step: [ plays a 11.77-second climbing video ](https://huggingface.co/HannesVonEssen/microduck-climb/resolve/main/media/preview.mp4). The same project provides climbing and standing strategies, ONNX, PPO checkpoints, environment code, and ladder models: [ models and demonstration pages ](https://huggingface.co/HannesVonEssen/microduck-climb) · [ training and reproduction code ](https://github.com/Vottivott/microduck-playground/tree/main/experiments/desk-climb). For a replay of the local rung contact phase in this topic, see the “Ladder Climbing” entry below.

The community also released a policy with eight levels of stilts ranging from 10 cm to 2 m, each level including independent videos, ONNX, and training checkpoints: [ Stilt Policy and Video Collection ](https://huggingface.co/HannesVonEssen/microduck-stilts). Among them, [ 200 cm simulation video ](https://huggingface.co/HannesVonEssen/microduck-stilts/resolve/main/200cm/preview.mp4) demonstrates alternating support walking.

## Materials and Reproduction

- All submitted video previews are in GIF format; the MP4 files in Notebook outputs have been replaced by relative GIF links.
- The original MP4 files do not enter the main repository, reducing cloning and browsing overhead. Details on the environment, model, metrics, and full replay instructions for each task can be found in the corresponding task README.
- The board-side task videos for RDK X5 are independent reasoning per task; Ubuntu is responsible for physical simulation and encoding, while BPU handles action reasoning. Videos marked as “saved” can be previewed directly; BPU units running the Notebook can generate new board-side closed-loop videos.
